comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE PROVEN: THE LOCK BUMP IS IMPOSSIBLE. THE CAP COMES FROM inspect-ai, NOT FROM US.

This settles which remediation option is available, so it should not be re-litigated. Established by
DIRECT EXPERIMENT, not inference: I temporarily added 'constraint-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]'
under [tool.uv] and ran 'uv lock'. It is UNSATISFIABLE, and uv named the culprit:

    No solution found when resolving dependencies for split
    (python_full_version >= '3.14' and sys_platform == 'win32'):
    Because inspect-ai>=0.3.221 depends on one of:
        click>=8.1.3,<8.2.0
        click>8.2.0,<8.2.2
    and click>=8.3.3, we can conclude that inspect-ai>=0.3.221 cannot be used.

So inspect-ai CAPS click below 8.2.2 across the available versions (it enumerated up to 0.3.242).
inspect-ai arrives via the [eval] extra, and uv's UNIVERSAL resolution locks every extra jointly —
the mechanism pyproject.toml:250-256 already documents for the boto3 diamond. The working tree was
restored immediately afterwards; 'git status --porcelain' is clean and neither pyproject.toml nor
uv.lock is modified.

WHY THE EARLIER ATTEMPTS LOOKED INERT. 'uv lock --upgrade-package click' (and with
--refresh-package) reported success and left 8.2.1, changing only an unrelated zipfile-zstd marker.
That is NOT a stale cache and NOT the uv-version mismatch I had hypothesised: --upgrade-package only
PERMITS a move within the existing constraint set, and 8.2.1 remains the newest click that satisfies
inspect-ai's cap. So the no-op was the resolver being correct, and my resolver-version hypothesis is
RETRACTED — recording that rather than leaving a wrong lead in the ticket.

THEREFORE OPTION 1 (minimal lock bump to >= 8.3.3) IS RULED OUT. It cannot be done without
removing or downgrading inspect-ai, i.e. dropping the [eval] extra's framework, which is far more
invasive than the advisory warrants and is not this ticket's business.

OPTION 2 IS THE PATH, AND IT IS NOW GENUINELY JUSTIFIED RATHER THAN A SHRUG. The justification has
three legs, each verifiable:
 1. click is a TRANSITIVE dependency — 'git grep "import click"' over src returns NOTHING; rebar
    never imports it.
 2. PYSEC-2026-2132 is a command-injection in click.edit() specifically, and 'click.edit' appears
    NOWHERE in src, tests or scripts. The vulnerable code path is unreachable in this project.
 3. The cap is UPSTREAM and outside our control: inspect-ai pins click < 8.2.2. We cannot fix this by
    choosing better versions.
So the ignore is not 'we would rather not deal with it' — it is 'the advisory does not apply to this
project, and the version that fixes it is unreachable while inspect-ai is a dependency'.

REQUIRED SHAPE OF THE IGNORE, so it cannot rot into a blanket suppression:
 * scope it to the ONE advisory id (--ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-2132), never a broad skip, and keep the
   pip-audit job GATING;
 * an inline comment recording all three legs above AND a REMOVE-WHEN condition: remove this ignore
   as soon as inspect-ai relaxes its click cap enough for the lock to carry click >= 8.3.3
   (re-test with the constraint experiment above — it is cheap and decisive);
 * greppable, so the next person auditing suppressions finds it with the advisory id.

WORTH FILING SEPARATELY (not here, and not blocking): nothing currently tells us WHEN inspect-ai
relaxes that cap, so the ignore could outlive its justification silently. A periodic re-test — the
same one-line constraint experiment — would catch it. That is a hygiene follow-up, not part of
unblocking.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION + RESOLUTION: option 1 (bump click in the lock) IS possible and is now implemented. An earlier comment on this ticket concluded option 1 was impossible; that conclusion was based on `constraint-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]` returning UNSATISFIABLE. That experiment cannot decide the question: uv constraint-dependencies only NARROWS an existing constraint set, so it can never lift inspect-ai s cap and UNSATISFIABLE was the expected outcome. The correct tool is `override-dependencies`, which REPLACES the offending requirement. Result: `uv lock` -> "Resolved 167 packages. Updated click v8.2.1 -> v8.4.2".

ROOT CAUSE (agreed, independently proven twice): inspect-ai (via the [eval] extra) requires `click!=8.2.0,<8.2.2,>=8.1.3`, and uv resolves all extras jointly, so 8.2.1 is genuinely the newest click satisfying the set. Proof: deleting the inspect-ai line from pyproject and relocking moves click to 8.4.2 immediately. The uv-version / resolver-mismatch hypothesis is NOT the cause; `uv lock --upgrade-package click` was a no-op because it only permits movement inside the existing constraints.

NO inspect-ai release relaxes the cap - it is identical across every version through the latest 0.3.251. Upstream PR UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai#4596 (issue #4594) is open to relax it, unmerged. So waiting for upstream is not an option.

THE CAP IS STALE, NOT A REAL INCOMPATIBILITY - tested directly: inspect-ai 0.3.251 installed with click 8.4.2 imports cleanly, and `inspect --help` and `inspect eval --help` both render and exit 0. This is what makes the override safe rather than reckless.

FIX: [tool.uv] override-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"] in pyproject.toml + relocked uv.lock. The override governs this repo s lock/envs only and is NOT published in nava-rebar wheel metadata, so no consumer resolve is affected. pyproject carries the full rationale and a REMOVE-WHEN (drop it once inspect-ai ships a release admitting click >= 8.3.3).

VERIFICATION: `uv lock --check` passes under BOTH uv 0.7.18 and uv 0.12.1 (lock stays at revision 2, so CI-safe whatever setup-uv v9 installs); `uv sync --locked --extra dev` resolves and installs click 8.4.2; `pip-audit --desc` over that whole environment reports "No known vulnerabilities found", so the old pin was masking nothing else; 1463 selected tests pass, 0 failures.

DIFF SCOPE: click 8.2.1->8.4.2, the lock manifest override line, and one stale zipfile-zstd marker that any relock corrects (uv 0.7.18 and 0.12.1 agree on it). The other 166 packages are untouched.

Option 2 (--ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-2132) is therefore NOT needed and is deliberately declined: it would suppress a real advisory and weaken a gating security check when a clean fix exists.

comments.body:
*** CORRECTION TO MY PREVIOUS COMMENT: ITS CONCLUSION IS WRONG. OPTION 1 IS FEASIBLE. DO NOT ACT ON
THE 'OPTION 1 IS RULED OUT / OPTION 2 IS THE PATH' PARAGRAPHS ABOVE. ***

MY ERROR, precisely. I tested feasibility with 'constraint-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]'.
constraint-dependencies can only NARROW an existing constraint set — it cannot LIFT a cap that an
upstream package declares. So against inspect-ai's 'click>=8.1.3,<8.2.0 | >8.2.0,<8.2.2' the
UNSATISFIABLE result was the EXPECTED output of that tool, and it says nothing about whether the
upgrade is achievable. I read a tool limitation as a property of the dependency graph and recorded
the conclusion as established. The root-cause half of that comment stands (inspect-ai is the capper;
the uv-version hypothesis is retracted); the REMEDIATION half does not.

THE CORRECT TOOL IS override-dependencies, WHICH REPLACES THE OFFENDING REQUIREMENT:

    [tool.uv]
    override-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]

'uv lock' -> 'Resolved 167 packages. Updated click v8.2.1 -> v8.4.2'. Fully satisfiable. Found and
verified by the agent implementing this ticket, which also independently confirmed the root cause by
deleting inspect-ai from pyproject and watching click jump to 8.4.2.

WHY THE OVERRIDE IS DEFENSIBLE AND NOT JUST A BIGGER HAMMER — the cap is STALE, not a real
incompatibility:
 * inspect-ai 0.3.251 (the latest) imports cleanly under click 8.4.2, and 'inspect --help' and
   'inspect eval --help' both render and exit 0.
 * NO inspect-ai release ever relaxes the cap, up to 0.3.251 — so waiting is not a strategy.
 * Upstream is already fixing it: UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai PR #4596 against issue #4594, still
   unmerged. That is the REMOVE-WHEN condition for the override.

VERIFICATION ALREADY PASSED, and it is the part that matters:
 * 'uv lock --check' passes under BOTH uv 0.7.18 and uv 0.12.1, and the lock stays at revision 2 —
   so it is CI-safe whichever uv 'setup-uv v9' installs. (This also disposes of my resolver-version
   hypothesis for good.)
 * 'uv sync --locked --extra dev' resolves and installs click 8.4.2.
 * 'pip-audit --desc' over that whole environment: 'No known vulnerabilities found' — so the old pin
   was masking nothing else, which was the specific risk I asked to have checked.
 * Diff is minimal: click 8.2.1->8.4.2, the manifest override line, and the one stale zipfile-zstd
   marker that any relock corrects (uv 0.7.18 and 0.12.1 agree on it). The other 166 packages are
   untouched.

SO OPTION 2 IS WITHDRAWN. Suppressing PYSEC-2026-2132 would have weakened a gating security check to
work around a stale upstream pin that can simply be overridden — the wrong trade, and I had
pre-authorised it on a proof that did not hold. The implementer declined it and was right to.

FILE-IMPACT NOTE: uv.lock stays in file_impact (I had wrongly told the implementer to drop it), and
pyproject.toml is legitimately needed too, since the lock cannot carry click >= 8.3.3 without the
override declaration. Both were already declared before any review ran, so nothing is staled.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SCOPE OF THE OVERRIDE (recording here so it is on the ticket, not just in chat): `[tool.uv] override-dependencies` is a WORKSPACE RESOLUTION DIRECTIVE. It is consumed by uv when resolving/locking THIS repo and is NOT published in nava-rebar wheel metadata. Consequences:

* A consumer running `pip install nava-rebar[eval]` from PyPI is UNAFFECTED - they still get inspect-ai s own `click!=8.2.0,<8.2.2,>=8.1.3` cap and resolve click 8.2.1. Behaviour unchanged for them; we have not pushed a click floor onto downstream users.
* The override moves ONLY this repo s committed uv.lock and the envs synced from it (CI, contributor worktrees).

So the blast radius is this repo s own environments, which is exactly where the gating pip-audit job runs.

CI COVERAGE OF inspect-ai UNDER THE NEW LOCK - nothing in CI exercises it, and it is STRUCTURALLY unable to:
1. inspect-ai is only in the `[eval]` extra. The pip-audit job installs `uv sync --locked --extra dev` (no eval), so inspect-ai is not installed there; click 8.4.2 reaches the audited set via uvicorn and other dev deps, not via inspect-ai.
2. pyproject `[tool.uv] conflicts` declares `[{extra="eval"}, {extra="dev"}]` mutually conflicting ("nothing installs dev+eval together"). The pytest suite runs off the dev extra, so inspect-ai CANNOT be present in the tested set - this is not "we happened not to test it".
3. rebar imports inspect_ai lazily behind `guard_import(..., extra="eval")`, so those paths abstain when it is absent.
4. 1463 selected tests pass under the new lock, 0 failures.

HONEST LIMIT ON THE STALENESS EVIDENCE: I verified inspect-ai 0.3.251 imports under click 8.4.2 and that `inspect --help` / `inspect eval --help` render and exit 0 - that exercises click s Command/Option construction and the group->subcommand dispatch chain, which is where an 8.2.2+ API break (BaseCommand/MultiCommand removal, parser/context changes) would raise. I did NOT run a live eval task end-to-end (needs model credentials). Tracked as a follow-up ticket, discovered_from this one; the gap PREDATES this change.

ON THE zipfile-zstd MARKER in the lock diff: not caused by the override. inspect-ai requires zipfile-zstd only under `python_full_version < 3.14`, and zipfile-zstd unconditionally requires `zstandard>=0.15.0`; uv propagates the parent marker down to that transitive edge. Both uv 0.7.18 and 0.12.1 emit it, so the committed lock was simply stale on it and ANY relock corrects it. It narrows zstandard s marker to exactly the range where its only requirer is installed - no change to the installed set on any Python CI tests (3.11/3.12/3.13).

compiled_state.description:
# The gating pip-audit job fails on EVERY Gerrit patchset, blocking all Verified +1 votes

## Symptom

`build-and-test / pip-audit (dependency vulnerabilities)` fails on every patchset run
observed today, so no change can reach `Verified +1`. Confirmed across five independent
runs on different agents' patchsets: 30770494611, 30770603146, 30770604307, 30770971365,
30771122330, 30771131391. All share head sha 4214516f95 (`origin/main`), and the failures
are identical, so this is a property of `main`, not of any one change.

## Root cause — a real advisory, NOT a network flake

From run 30770494611's job log (the audit step's own output):

    pip-audit attempt 1/3
    click 8.2.1   PYSEC-2026-2132   8.3.3   Pallets Click, versions 8.3.2 and below,
      contain a command injection vulnerability in the click.edit() function, allowing
      attackers to pass arbitrary OS commands from an unprivileged account.
    ##[error]pip-audit found dependency vulnerabilities (see output). Bump the pinned
      version, or add --ignore-vuln <ID> with justification if accepted.

It succeeded on attempt 1 — it REACHED the advisory DB and found a vulnerability. So the
workflow's documented infra escape hatch does NOT apply: `_build-and-test.yml`'s failure
policy reserves `recheck` for the case where all three attempts fail to reach the DB.
Commenting `recheck` will not clear this.

`click` is a TRANSITIVE dependency pinned at 8.2.1 in the committed `uv.lock` (line 711);
it is not pinned in `pyproject.toml`. The advisory appears to have been published after
`ce5d: go uv-canonical with a committed lock` landed the lock, which is why a previously
green gate went red with no code change.

## Remediation (one of)

1. Refresh the lock so `click` resolves to >= 8.3.3 (the fix version pip-audit names).
   Preferred: it removes the vulnerability rather than accepting it.
2. If 8.3.3 is not resolvable under the current constraint set, `--ignore-vuln
   PYSEC-2026-2132` with a written justification, per the failure policy's explicit
   provision for that (`_build-and-test.yml`, "Failure policy"). Note rebar does not call
   `click.edit()`, so the exploit path is plausibly not reachable — but that argument
   belongs IN the justification comment, reviewed, not assumed here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pip-audit` is green on a fresh patchset against `main`
- [ ] the fix is a lock/pin change or a justified, greppable `--ignore-vuln`, not a
      blanket skip of the job
- [ ] if option 2 is taken, the justification names why the vulnerable code path is
      unreachable from rebar

## Why this is filed separately

Discovered while landing story 79d5 (DC length convergence), whose diff is two new test
files plus a source comment and touches no dependency pin. A lock refresh is a different
change with a different blast radius, and `uv.lock` is outside that story's declared file
impact.

file_impact.reason: Relock so click resolves to 8.4.2 (>= the PYSEC-2026-2132 fix version 8.3.3) instead of the vulnerable 8.2.1; records the uv override in the lock manifest. Only click changes, plus one stale zipfile-zstd marker any relock corrects.

Add [tool.uv] override-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"] with the rationale and a REMOVE-WHEN. Required because inspect-ai caps click<8.2.2, which pins the universal resolution to the vulnerable 8.2.1 and makes a lock-only bump impossible.

compiled_state.title: pip-audit gate is red on main: click 8.2.1 PYSEC-2026-2132
